summary: The study describes the thermal ALD growth of metallic titanium films using titanium tetrachloride and 1,4-bis(trimethylsilyl)-2-methyl-2,5-cyclohexadiene or 1,4-bis(trimethylsilyl)-1,4-dihydropyrazine as reducing agents. The process was optimized with specific pulse sequences and temperature ranges to achieve conformal and uniform film growth. The films oxidized upon exposure to air, and XPS analysis confirmed the presence of titanium metal in the bulk of the films.
evidence: The growth of electropositive metal films from chemical precursors is extremely challenging... Due to the very small feature sizes and three-dimensional architectures of future transistors, titanium metal must be deposited by atomic layer deposition (ALD) to meet thickness uniformity and conformality requirements. Herein, we describe the low temperature ALD growth of metallic titanium films using TiCl4 and 1 and 2 as precursors. The studies described herein were carried out on Si(100) with native oxide and thermal SiO2 (100 nm)/Si substrates. An ALD window was observed from 110 to 240 °C... These data confirm the presence of Ti(0) in the bulk of the film.
